name: og-06-chemistry-to-heredity
title: Chemistry to heredity (Campaign VI)
question: Does inherited state improve persistence/throughput — comparing RNA-like, peptide-assisted, compositional and hybrid heredity — rather than template replication in isolation? (Do NOT presume RNA.)
hypothesis: At least one heredity module raises lineage persistence + information retention above its non-heritable control under a feasible resource budget; the winner is not assumed a priori.
objective: Introduce competing heredity modules and test whether inherited state improves persistence under feasible budgets.
proposed_mechanisms: J: polymers, information and heredity (as competing modules)

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: inheritance-beats-noninheritance
behavior_tests.description: The RNA-like heredity module retains functional information and outscores the non-heritable control (whose function degrades away).

measure.detail: RNA-like lineage fitness at steady state

pass_if.detail: inheriting lineage fitness net-positive (and beats the non-heritable control)

behavior_tests.name: information-retained-above-error-threshold
behavior_tests.description: The RNA-like module sits above the Eigen error threshold — functional information is retained (C/(C+E) high), not lost to the error catastrophe.

pass_if.detail: functional information retained (above the error threshold)

behavior_tests.name: heredity-modules-compared
behavior_tests.description: Two viable heredity modules compared head-to-head: RNA-like (long, high-fidelity) outscores the cheaper, lower-fidelity peptide module — an evidence-based ranking, not assumed.

pass_if.detail: both modules viable; RNA-like ranks above peptide

behavior_tests.name: error-catastrophe-below-threshold
behavior_tests.description: Discriminating (Eigen): below the error threshold (low fidelity × long sequence) functional information is lost — retention collapses and inheritance fails.

behavior_tests.name: replication-feasible-budget
behavior_tests.description: Inheritance pays within a feasible replication budget — net-positive fitness after the replication cost, not idealized.

literature_anchors.expectation: Mineral/CO-driven peptide formation at 100 C, pH 7-10
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Not yet measurable — module processes not built

claim: An inherited (replicable) polymer state improves lineage fitness above its replication cost IF fidelity beats the Eigen error threshold — RNA-like (long, high-fidelity) wins a head-to-head against a cheaper peptide module, and both beat the non-heritable control; below the threshold information is lost (error catastrophe).
result: RNA-like fitness 0.38 (retention 0.62) > peptide 0.24 > non-heritable ~0; the low-fidelity module collapses (retention 0, fitness −0.10).

findings.statement: A high-fidelity heredity module (RNA-like, 30-mer, per-site fidelity 0.99 → whole-sequence Q=0.74) retains functional information (C/(C+E)=0.62) and achieves net-positive lineage fitness (0.38) after its replication cost, outscoring the non-heritable control whose function degrades away.
findings.explanation: Real libRoadRunner quasispecies ODE; above the Eigen error threshold correct templates outreplicate the mutational error tail.

findings.statement: Heredity modules rank by an evidence-based head-to-head — RNA-like (0.38) beats the cheaper, lower-fidelity peptide module (0.24), and both beat non-inheritance — while a module below the error threshold (per-site 0.90 × 30-mer, Q=0.04) suffers the error catastrophe (retention 0, fitness −0.10).
findings.explanation: Whole-sequence fidelity Q = per_site_fidelity^length sets the threshold; longer high-fidelity polymers retain more information but cost more to replicate.
findings.next_action: Couple the winning heredity module to the og-02 network to test whether inherited catalysts raise metabolic throughput.

report.title: Campaign VI — chemistry to heredity
report.verdict: PASS — inheritance pays above the error threshold; modules ranked head-to-head
report.main_insight: An inherited polymer state improves lineage fitness above its replication cost only where fidelity beats the Eigen error threshold; RNA-like wins a head-to-head against a cheaper peptide module, and a sub-threshold module suffers the error catastrophe.
report.conclusion: The real libRoadRunner quasispecies replicator shows the heredity transition: inheritance is favored above the error threshold and ranked by an evidence-based head-to-head, within a feasible replication budget. Opens the genetic era of the campaign (og-07 ecology, og-08 escape).
report.caveat: The functional "benefit" and replication "cost" are reduced couplings; the quasispecies is the real Eigen ODE (libRoadRunner), the fidelity/length error threshold first-principles.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces the Eigen error threshold — inheritance pays above it, collapses below it — and ranks two viable modules head-to-head.

explanatory_gain.basis: The quasispecies ODE explains both the information-retention transition and the fidelity × length threshold from first principles.

limitations: The functional benefit and replication cost are reduced couplings; only the quasispecies dynamics are the real engine.
Two heredity modules compared (RNA-like, peptide); a broader module library is deferred.

resolved_uncertainties: Inheritance improves fitness above the Eigen error threshold and can be ranked across modules by an evidence-based head-to-head.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether an inherited catalyst actually raises the og-02 network's metabolic throughput in-lineage.

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Couple the winning heredity module to the og-02 rTCA network; measure inherited-catalyst throughput gain.

key_assumptions: Treat informational chemistry as a branch point; do not presume a viable RNA replication mechanism.
expert_questions: Which heredity modules to prioritize first: RNA-world, peptide-first, compositional, or mineral-surface templating?
